subject: Biology
title: Antibiotic Resistance
description: A quick win: understand Antibiotic Resistance.

hook.text: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928. It saved millions. But bacteria are fighting back.

buildup.text: Overuse of antibiotics in medicine and farming gives resistant bacteria an advantage.

discovery.text: MRSA—methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus—shrugs off drugs that once killed it easily.

twist.text: Bacteria share resistance genes with each other, even across species, spreading immunity fast.

climax.text: Without new antibiotics, routine surgeries and minor infections could become deadly again.

punchline.text: We gave bacteria a challenge. They adapted.

quiz.question: How do bacteria spread antibiotic resistance?
options: By sharing resistance genes across species

details.summary: Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria evolve mechanisms to survive antibiotic treatment. Overuse and misuse of antibiotics accelerate resistance by selecting for resistant mutants. The WHO calls it one of the greatest threats to global health, food security, and development.
details.whyItMatters: Resistant infections already kill over 1.2 million people annually. Without new antibiotics or strategies, common infections and routine surgeries could become life-threatening again, returning medicine to a pre-antibiotic era.
takeaways: Resistant bacteria survive antibiotic treatment and pass resistance genes to offspring
Over 1.2 million people die annually from antibiotic-resistant infections
Resistance genes spread between species via horizontal gene transfer on plasmids

faq.question: How do bacteria become resistant to antibiotics?
faq.answer: Through random mutations that alter drug targets, produce enzymes that destroy the antibiotic, or pump the drug out of the cell. When antibiotics kill susceptible bacteria, resistant mutants survive and multiply. Resistance genes also spread between species on mobile plasmids.

faq.question: What can individuals do to combat antibiotic resistance?
faq.answer: Complete prescribed antibiotic courses fully. Never use antibiotics for viral infections like colds. Do not share or save leftover antibiotics. Practice good hygiene to prevent infections. Support policies that reduce antibiotic use in agriculture.
